info.name: Garrison
info.description:
Garrison REST, A2A, and MCP APIs (v0.3.0).

Select the Garrison environment, start a server and a worker that has `garrison-fake-harness` on its PATH, and run the collection top to bottom. The Auth folder signs in and stores a session token that every later request uses; the folders in between create resources with unique names and exercise every REST route; Cleanup deletes them again. The last folder restarts the server, so leave it out against shared servers.

Every path and method in the server's OpenAPI document (`GET /openapi.json`, the second request in Auth) has at least one request here, and each request's description ends with its route, the permission it needs, what it answers, and the errors to expect. Routes reached through URLs another call returns (the artifact, asset, and file download tickets) are followed from those responses. The app gateway's file stream never ends on its own, so the collection checks its refusal instead of reading it.

Environment variables (Garrison.postman_environment.json):

- `baseUrl`: the REST listener, for example `http://127.0.0.1:8700`.
- `mcpUrl`: the MCP endpoint, for example `http://127.0.0.1:8701/mcp`.
- `tenantId`: the tenant the collection works in (`default`).
- `email` and `password`: the user Auth signs in as.
- `adminApiKey`: the administrator API key, sent as `x-api-key` by the requests that show it.
- `accessKey` and `secretKey`: a credential for the key-based token and the signed request.
- `nodeAccessKey` and `nodeSecretKey`: the worker credential the Node Protocol folder uses.

Identifiers created along the way are collection variables; each one's description says which request sets it and where it is used. A few have defaults you can change: `providerApiSmokeEnabled` and the `providerApi...` values for the opt-in provider smoke folder, the `inference...` values for the inference examples, and the `missing...Id` values the 404 checks use.

See REST_API.md, MCP_API.md, A2A_API.md, and WEBSOCKETS_API.md in the repository for the full reference.

item.name: Auth
item.description: Authentication comes first: every later request uses the session token captured here (collection-level bearer auth). Also shows the other schemes: credential keys, header-based login, the administrator API key, and a signed request.

request.description:
Anonymous readiness check (same as /v1.0/api/health/ready). Answers 200 when the database answers, its schema is current, and the replica is not draining; 503 otherwise.

`GET /v1.0/api/health`: Readiness: 200 when the database answers, the schema is current, and the replica is not draining; 503 otherwise. No credentials needed. Success: 200 with `HealthResponse`.

The live OpenAPI 3.0 document, generated from the same route registrations the server serves. The dashboard's API Explorer reads it, and so can any OpenAPI tool. No credentials are needed, and it lists every REST route this collection exercises.

`GET /openapi.json`: The OpenAPI 3.0 document for every REST route. No credentials needed. Success: 200.

item.name: Pipelines
item.description: Pipelines run agents as ordered stages on one request: each stage is an ordinary run of its agent, sees the earlier stages' results through its PipelineStage prompt template, and can wait for a person to approve, request changes, or reject. This folder creates a two-stage pipeline on the Postman agent, runs it through a revision and an approval, exercises cancel, retry, and the 409 cases, and deletes everything it made, so it must run before Cleanup deletes the agent. Definitions need Pipeline permissions, pipeline runs need PipelineRun, and stage reviews need Read or Update on Approval. Run tokens cannot use any of these routes. See docs/PIPELINES.md and the Pipelines section of REST_API.md.

request.description:
Creates a pipeline with two stages on the Postman agent. Stages run in list order and get positions 1 and 2. The first stage pins the deployment so it can pass the run parameter format (parameters are checked against that deployment's allowedRunOverrides when the pipeline is saved) and requires a review with at most one revision. The second stage uses the agent's weighted deployment selection and may run twice when it fails. Needs Create on Pipeline. Validation failures answer 400 ValidationFailed with field codes such as PipelineEmpty, TooManyStages, ReferenceNotFound, DeploymentAgentMismatch, and TemplateKindMismatch; a duplicate name answers 409 NameConflict.

item.description: Permission approvals. When a deployment has approvalsEnabled, Claude Code and Codex app-server runs relay permission prompts to Garrison; the deployment's approval rules decide each request or send it to a person, and the run stays Running (awaitingApproval true) until someone decides or the approval expires. Reading needs Read on Approval; deciding needs Update on Approval.

request.description:
Replaces the deployment with approval settings: an ordered rule list (Deny beats Ask, Ask beats Allow), the default action for requests no rule matches, and the timeout. approvalsEnabled stays false because the fake harness profile cannot relay approvals (only Claude Code profiles and Codex profiles with CodexAppServer delivery accept true); the rules can still be tested with approval-check. item.name: Mandates
item.description: Keepers (mandates, AA1): an agent with a standing job that wakes on a schedule. Each wake is a tick, one run of the keeper's deployment; only one tick runs at a time. Changes to the objective and schedule are revisions, published to take effect. A keeper runs as the principal that last created or changed it, so creating one needs Execute on its agent.

request.description:
Creates a keeper (mandate) on the Postman agent and deployment. The inline currentRevision is published as revision 1, so the keeper starts Active and its first wake is scheduled. minIntervalSeconds 10 is below the cluster floor Autonomy.MinIntervalSeconds (60 by default), so the stored value is raised and the response lists a ValueClamped warning. Needs Create on Mandate and Execute on the agent; the caller becomes the principal its ticks run as. A remote agent answers 400 RemoteAgentUnsupported; a duplicate name answers 409 NameConflict.

`POST /v1.0/api/tenants/{tenantId}/mandates`: Create a mandate (needs Agent Execute; the caller becomes its run-as principal). An inline currentRevision is published as revision 1 and the mandate becomes Active. Needs Create on `Mandate`. Body: `Mandate`. Success: 201 with `Mandate`. Errors: 400 when the body fails validation, 401 without a valid token, 403 without the permission.

item.name: Escalations
item.description: Escalations (AA2): questions a run raises for a person, a role, or another agent when it should not decide alone, with optional options, a default answer, a severity, and a timeout. Runs raise and withdraw them over MCP (garrison_escalate, garrison_withdraw_escalation); people list, read, answer, and cancel them here. Non-blocking escalations let the run continue; a Blocking one suspends its run until answered. The escalations WebSocket channel streams them.

item.name: Draft revision with a default escalation target

request.description:
